summary: Phase F2 (Login 2FA + lockout + session + audit) backend testing. 17 of 18 pytest cases pass end-to-end against the public preview URL. Verified: two-step login envelope (challenge_token 64 chars, no access_token in step 1, correct field types), OTP queued mail written to storage/logs/laravel.log by laravel-queue, verify() returns Bearer + UUID-v7 PAT id + user/roles/128 permissions + expires_at ~480min ahead, PAT row in personal_access_tokens has matching UUID id and expires_at ~8h ahead (SANCTUM_TOKEN_EXPIRATION=480), OTP single-use replay is rejected, 5 wrong OTPs decrement remaining_attempts then destroy the challenge on the 6th call, OTP expiry via tinker rejects the challenge, resend has a 60s cooldown returning retry_after_seconds, clearing last_sent_at issues a NEW code while keeping the SAME challenge_token, resets attempts to 5 and decrements remaining_resends (3->2->1->0), old code no longer verifies, resend limit of 3 is enforced, 5 wrong passwords lock the account (statuses 401,401,401,401,423 with decreasing remaining_attempts), users.failed_login_attempts=5 and locked_until is populated, 6th wrong password AND the CORRECT password both return 423 with locked_until + retry_after_seconds while the lock is active, successful password auth resets failed_login_attempts to 0, enumeration protection returns identical 'These credentials do not match our records.' for unknown email and wrong password, is_active=0 returns 403 'This account has been deactivated.', validation returns the standard 422 envelope with per-field errors for login and two-factor/verify, /me returns user+roles+128 permissions, /logout revokes only the current PAT (subsequent /me = 401 Unauthenticated.), /logout-all revokes every PAT and reports revoked_tokens, audit rows exist in activity_logs for all 8 required actions (two_factor_issued, two_factor_verified, two_factor_failed, login_failed, account_locked, account_locked_out, login_succeeded, logged_out) with ip_address and new_values populated. Regression: /api/v1/health still healthy and unknown routes still return the JSON 404 envelope. ONE CRITICAL BUG FOUND: the login rate limiter returns HTTP 500 instead of 429 - see below.

critical.issue: Rate limiter throws HTTP 500 (TypeError) instead of returning the documented 429 JSON envelope. AppServiceProvider::configureRateLimiters() declares the response callback as `fn (Request $request, int $seconds = 60) => ...` but Laravel 11/12 invokes it as `$responseCallback($request, $headers)` where `$headers` is an ARRAY (see vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Routing/Middleware/ThrottleRequests.php line 253). Reproduction: `for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -X POST $BASE/api/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"x@y.z","password":"bad"}' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'; done` returns 401,401,401,500,500,500,500,500,500,500. laravel.log shows: 'TypeError: Argument #2 ($seconds) must be of type int, array given, called in .../ThrottleRequests.php on line 253 at .../AppServiceProvider.php:35'. Impact: legitimate rate-limit rejections leak stack traces, the Retry-After header is not sent, and clients cannot distinguish DoS mitigation from server bugs. This affects auth-login (5/min), auth-two-factor (10/min), auth-two-factor-resend (3/min) and the generic api limiter (120/min).

action_items: Fix AppServiceProvider::configureRateLimiters() closure signature. Change `fn (Request $request, int $seconds = 60) => ApiResponse::error('Too many requests. Please try again later.', 429)->header('Retry-After', $seconds)` to accept the headers array Laravel actually passes, e.g. `fn (Request $request, array $headers = []) => ApiResponse::error('Too many requests. Please try again later.', 429)->withHeaders($headers)` (or compute Retry-After from $headers['Retry-After'] ?? 60). Once fixed, TestRateLimiting.test_login_throttle_shape should turn green (it currently sees 500 instead of 429).
critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL: RateLimiter response callback signature mismatch (see backend_issues.critical). Same buggy closure is reused for all four named limiters so all throttled endpoints will 500 on burst instead of 429.
Nice: AuthenticationService uses a constant DUMMY_HASH to keep timing constant when a user does not exist - good enumeration defence.
Nice: after 5 failed OTP attempts the challenge row is deleted and subsequent calls with the same challenge_token get 422 telling the user to sign in again - correctly documented and tested.
Nice: personal_access_tokens uses UUID-v7 ids and Sanctum expires_at is enforced (~480 minutes verified in DB and in the response body).
Nice: activity_logs captures every required auth.* event with ip_address + new_values; masked_email is used in the login step 1 response so full addresses are never echoed.

Minor observation (not a bug for F2): TestOtpWrongCode confirmed the challenge row is deleted after the 5th wrong code, so the 6th attempt returns 422 'The verification code is invalid.' rather than a more explicit 'sign in again' message. Consider a 401/410 with a clearer 'challenge expired, please sign in again' body if UX allows.

Minor: the successful login-succeeded event is only recorded when a token is issued (i.e. after verifyChallenge or when 2FA is disabled), which means step 1 password success is not itself audited except via the subsequent two_factor_issued row. That is fine and matches the spec.
Minor: `_reset_user_lock` teardown is safe to run repeatedly; the test suite is idempotent and leaves editor.test@adiprimanto.com with failed_login_attempts=0 and locked_until=NULL after every run.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase F2 auth is functionally correct except for one 500-instead-of-429 bug in AppServiceProvider::configureRateLimiters (documented above). After the main agent fixes the closure signature, rerun `python -m pytest backend/tests/pytest/test_phase_f2_auth.py -v` and expect 18/18. The test file uses direct MySQL/tinker to bypass timing gates (OTP TTL, resend cooldown, throttle cache); it calls `php artisan cache:clear` between tests to reset the rate limiter counters so tests don't interfere with each other. Editor account is the destructive account - super admin should never be locked. Total run time ~90s.
rca of the issue: TypeError in AppServiceProvider::configureRateLimiters() closure. Laravel 11/12 signature for RateLimiter::for(...)->response($cb) invokes `$cb($request, array $headers)` (see Illuminate\Routing\Middleware\ThrottleRequests::buildException at line 253). The current code types the second argument as `int $seconds = 60`, so when Laravel finally builds the 429 response it passes an array and PHP throws TypeError -> ApiExceptionRenderer converts to HTTP 500. Reproduction: 6+ POSTs/min to /api/v1/auth/login for the same email+IP -> 500 with stack trace in storage/logs/laravel.log. Mitigation: change the closure to `fn (Request $request, array $headers = []) => ApiResponse::error('Too many requests. Please try again later.', 429)->withHeaders($headers)`. Apply to all four RateLimiter::for entries (auth-login, auth-two-factor, auth-two-factor-resend, api).
